# Matching payments by idempotency key

> Every night, the reconciliation job streams Stripe charges and matches them against our Payment records by idempotency key, recording any mismatches for investigation.

_Part of [Daily Stripe reconciliation](daily-reconciliation.md)_

Every night at 02:30 UTC, the `payments.reconcile-daily` job streams Stripe payment charges from the past day and compares them with our payment records, matching each one by idempotency key. Stripe stores the key in the payment intent's metadata as `idempotencyKey`; we store it in our `Payment` record. The job loads all our COMPLETED payments for that day indexed by their key, then streams Stripe charges one at a time (using constant memory). For each charge that succeeded and has a matching key, it looks up our Payment record and compares the amounts. Any mismatch gets recorded in the `ReconciliationIssue` table: either a Stripe charge we don't have a record for (`MISSING_IN_LEDGER`), a payment we recorded that Stripe doesn't know about (`MISSING_AT_PROVIDER`), or an amount difference (`AMOUNT_MISMATCH`). The job is idempotent per (provider, day). It upserts into `ReconciliationRun` at the start: if a run for that day already finished, the job exits immediately; if it crashed and reruns, the old issues are deleted and recalculated from scratch. This prevents duplicate issue records on retries and makes the job safe to reschedule.

**Look at:** [`ReconciliationJobs` in reconciliation.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/reconciliation.jobs.ts#L24)

## Pieces

- [The three types of reconciliation mismatches](reconciliation-issue-kinds.md): `MISSING_IN_LEDGER` means Stripe charged but we have no matching Payment record; `MISSING_AT_PROVIDER` means we have a record but Stripe never charged that key; `AMOUNT_MISMATCH` means both exist but the amounts differ.
- [ReconciliationRun: the idempotence mechanism](reconciliation-run-model.md): One row per (provider, day) pair; upserted at the start of each run. If `finishedAt` is already set, the job exits; if null, the job processes the day and sets `finishedAt` when done.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `ReconciliationRun` | One row per (provider, day); stores matched count, issue count, and `finishedAt` timestamp to track and idempotently gate reconciliation runs. |
| database | `ReconciliationIssue` | One row per detected mismatch; stores kind, idempotency key reference, and details as JSON (Stripe intent ID and amount, or just our amount). |
| database | `Payment` | Queried for COMPLETED records within the day, indexed by `idempotencyKey`; matched one-to-one against Stripe charges. |
| external | `Stripe Payment Intents API` | Streamed via `stripe.paymentIntentsCreatedBetween(from, to)`; yields each intent's `metadata.idempotencyKey` and amount in cents. |

## Watch out

- Intents without an `idempotencyKey` in metadata are silently skipped; if you charge Stripe without an idempotency key, that charge will never match and will be flagged as `MISSING_IN_LEDGER`.
- Only intents with status `succeeded` are checked; failed, pending, or canceled intents are ignored, so a charge that fails after the reconciliation day runs won't show up as a mismatch until later.
- Rerunning the job for a date that already finished is a no-op—it exits immediately without recalculating—so you can't re-verify issues once a run is marked done.
- Issues from previous runs are deleted before recalculation; there's no audit trail of what mismatches existed before, only the current state from the latest run.
